def test_controller():
    c = controller.Controller()
    
    # Initial state
    assert c.generation == 0
    assert c.busy == False
    assert c.rows == []

    gen1 = c.start()
    assert gen1 == 1
    assert c.busy == True
    
    # poll_status(1, 'queued')
    assert c.poll_status(1, 'queued') == False
    assert c.busy == True
    
    # poll_status(1, 'running')
    assert c.poll_status(1, 'running') == False
    assert c.busy == True
    
    # poll_status(1, 'completed') -> True ONCE
    assert c.poll_status(1, 'completed') == True
    
    # poll_status(1, 'completed') -> False (duplicate)
    assert c.poll_status(1, 'completed') == False
    
    # finish(1, rows) -> True once
    rows = [1, 2, 3]
    assert c.finish(1, rows) == True
    assert c.rows == [1, 2, 3]
    assert c.busy == False
    
    # finish(1, rows) -> False (already finished)
    assert c.finish(1, rows) == False

    # test preservation of rows and decisions across start()
    c.decisions['job1'] = 'done'
    c.rows = [4, 5]
    
    gen2 = c.start()
    assert gen2 == 2
    assert c.busy == True
    assert c.rows == [4, 5]
    assert c.decisions == {'job1': 'done'}
    
    # poll_status(2, 'completed') -> True ONCE
    assert c.poll_status(2, 'completed') == True
    
    # poll_status(2, 'completed') -> False
    assert c.poll_status(2, 'completed') == False
    
    # finish(2, rows2)
    rows2 = [6, 7]
    assert c.finish(2, rows2) == True
    assert c.rows == [6, 7]
    assert c.busy == False

    assert c.poll_status(1, 'failed') == False

    c.start() # gen 1
    assert c.poll_status(2, 'completed') == False
    assert c.poll_status(0, 'completed') == False
    
    # test unrequested finish
